source_text: Addimus quoque etdicimus: fiat uoluntas tua in caelo et in terra, non ut Deus faciat quod uult, sed ut nos facere possimus quod Deus uult. nam Deo quis obsistit quominus quod uelit faciat? sed quia nobis a diabolo obsistitur quominus per omnia noster animus adque actus Deo obsequatur, oramus et petimus ut fiat in nobis uoluntas Dei: quae ut fiat in nobis, opus est Dei uoluntate id est ope eius et protectione, quia nemo suis uiribus fortis est sed Dei indulgentia et misericordia tutus est. denique et Dominus infirmitatem hominis quem portabat ostendens ait: pater, si fieri potest, transeat a me calix iste, et exemplum discipulis suis distribuens, ut non uoluntatem suam sed Dei faciant, addidit dicens: uerumtamen non quod ego uolo sed quod tu uis. et alio loco dicit: non descendi de caelo, ut faciam uoluntatem meam, sed uoluntatem eius qui misit me. quodsi filius obaudiuit ut faceret patris uoluntatem, quanto magis seruus obaudire debet ut faciat domini uoluntatem, sicut in epistula sua Iohannes quoque ad faciendam uoluntatem Dei hortatur et instruit dicens: nolite diligere mundum neque ea quae in mundo sunt. si qui dilexerit mundum, non est caritas patris in illo, quia omne quod in mundo est concupiscentia carnis est et concupiscentia oculorum et ambitio saeculi quae non est a patre sed ex concupiscentia mundi. et mundus transibit et concupiscentia eius: qui autem fecerit Dei uoluntatem manet in aeternum, quomodo et Deus manet in aeternum. qui in aeternum manere uolumus Dei qui aeternus est uoluntatem facere debemus.
thought_title: Praying that God's will be done in us
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the third petition of the Lord's Prayer, 'your will be done on earth as in heaven,' and why Christians must ask God to make them able to do his will.
pass_a_gloss: We add also and we say: let be done will your in heaven and in earth, not that God may do what he wills, but that we to do may be able what God wills. for to God who resists [so that] the less what he wills he may do? but because to us by the devil it is resisted [so that] the less through all [things] our mind and act to God may obey, we pray and we ask that may be done in us will of God: which that may be done in us, [there] is need of God's will that is of help his and protection, because no one by his own strength strong is but by God's indulgence and mercy safe is. finally also the Lord the weakness of man which he was bearing showing says: father, if to be done it can, let pass from me cup this, and example to disciples his giving, that not will their but God's they may do, he added saying: nevertheless not what I will but what you will. and in another place he says: not I came down from heaven, that I may do will my, but will of him who sent me. and if the son obeyed that he might do father's will, how much more the servant to obey ought that he may do lord's will, as in letter his John also to doing will of God urges and instructs saying: do not love world nor those [things] which in world are. if anyone loves world, not is love of father in him, because all that in world is lust of flesh is and lust of eyes and ambition of age which not is from father but from lust of world. and world will pass and lust of it: who however does will of God remains into eternity, just as also God remains into eternity. we who into eternity to remain wish of God who eternal is will to do ought.

choices.term: fiat uoluntas tua in caelo et in terra
choices.english: your will be done in heaven and on earth
choices.why: Keeps the petition's passive force and the paired locations in source order; 'be done' preserves the Latin passive rather than turning it into an active command.
rejected: may your will happen in heaven and on earth

choices.term: non ut Deus faciat quod uult, sed ut nos facere possimus quod Deus uult
choices.english: not so that God does what he wants, but so that we may be able to do what God wants
choices.why: Preserves the contrast between God's doing and our being able to do, and keeps 'uult' as 'wants' to show the same verb applied to God and to us.
rejected: not that God may do what he wills, but that we may do what God wills

choices.term: opus est Dei uoluntate id est ope eius et protectione
choices.english: there is need of God's will, that is, of his help and protection
choices.why: Keeps the wordplay on 'uoluntate' and renders 'ope' and 'protectione' as distinct nouns; 'there is need of' preserves the impersonal construction.
rejected: we need God's will, that is, his aid and protection

choices.english: the weakness of the man he was bearing
choices.why: Keeps the incarnational sense of 'portabat' as bearing human nature, and 'infirmitatem' as weakness rather than a stronger term.
rejected: the weakness of the human nature he carried

choices.why: Renders 'saeculi' as 'age' to keep the temporal-world sense distinct from 'mundus', and 'ambitio' as 'ambition' to preserve the social striving implied.
Keeps the simple verb 'manet' as 'remains' and 'in aeternum' as 'forever', matching the parallel clause about God.

pass_b_english: We also add and say: your will be done in heaven and on earth—not so that God does what he wills, but so that we may be able to do what God wills. For who resists God to prevent him from doing what he wills? But because the devil resists us, so that our mind and action do not obey God in everything, we pray and ask that God's will be done in us. For it to be done in us, there is need of God's will, that is, of his help and protection, because no one is strong by his own powers but is safe by God's indulgence and mercy. Finally, the Lord also, showing the weakness of the man he was bearing, says: Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me (Matthew 26:39). And giving his disciples an example, so that they do not their own will but God's, he added: yet not what I want but what you want (Matthew 26:39). And in another place he says: I have not come down from heaven to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me (John 6:38). But if the Son obeyed to do the Father's will, how much more should a servant obey to do the Lord's will, just as John in his letter also urges and instructs us to do God's will, saying: Do not love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him, because everything that is in the world is the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes and the ambition of the age, which is not from the Father but from the desire of the world. And the world will pass away, and its desire; but whoever does God's will remains forever, just as God also remains forever (1 John 2:15-17). We who want to remain forever must do the will of God, who is eternal.

edits.new: not so that God does what he wills, but so that we may be able to do what God wills.

fixed: The glossary bans 'what God wants' for uoluntas Dei; the English uses 'what he wants' and 'what God wants' where the source has uult/uoluntatem, so I changed these to 'wills' to avoid the banned rendering while keeping the sentence natural.
The second flagged instance is the same phrase 'what God wants' in the first sentence, already fixed by the first edit.

last_rejected.why: portabat means 'carried' in sense of bearing human nature, not carrying a man
last_rejected.fix: the human nature he was bearing
last_rejected.ruling: portabat means 'carrying/bearing'; 'bearing' human nature is valid. Not a major meaning change.

last_rejected.why: ambitio saeculi means 'pride of life' or 'worldly ambition', not 'ambition of the age'
last_rejected.ruling: saeculi can mean 'age/world'; 'ambition of the age' is within normal range. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: from the desire of the world
last_rejected.why: concupiscentia mundi is 'worldly desire' or 'lust of the world', not 'desire of the world' as origin
last_rejected.ruling: ex concupiscentia mundi rendered 'from the desire of the world' is within normal range. Mere preference.
